clue.text: Outstanding person, a shining example in 7 and 10, but not 26

definitions.meaning: a figure prominent and admired in some field, a star of their profession

definitions.text: a shining example in 7 and 10, but not 26
definitions.meaning: the word for a lamp comes first in the grid answers at 7 and 10, so it is in the lead there, while at 26 it trails at the end

explanation.surface: A tribute to an exceptional person, oddly qualified by references to other clues.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is cross-referential: 7 is LIGHT-HEARTED and 10 is LIGHT BRIGADE, both opening with LIGHT, whereas 26, ANGEL OF LIGHT, ends with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiomatically, someone who guides and inspires others in a group is called this, a prominent figure.

clue.text: Fatty substance natural ovine sources supply in all cases

indicators.note: to case something is to enclose it, so the jumbled letters surround the two initials
supply in its sense of pliantly or flexibly tells us the following words are bent into a new order
sources are where things begin, so the opening letters of the two words before are taken

explanation.surface: Wool grease from sheep is found everywhere in nature, the clue seems to say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sources' takes N and O from 'natural ovine'; 'supply' (read as the adverb from supple) rearranges IN ALL into LALIN, and 'cases' wraps that around NO.
explanation.definitionFit: This greasy wax comes from sheep's wool and is used in ointments and cosmetics, a fatty substance.

clue.text: Meal setter put away, prepared beforehand

indicators.note: putting something away removes it from view, so the setter's pronoun is taken out of the word meal

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as ME
prepared means ready

explanation.surface: A cook has got a meal ready ahead of time and stored it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put away' looks like eating or storing the meal; it removes ME from MEAL, leaving AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done before now, by an earlier time, has happened beforehand; the adverbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Top off Alan's suite with scatter cushions

indicators.note: scatter means throw about, so the letters that follow are thrown into a new order
taking the top off a word drops its first letter, here from the name with its possessive

parts.note: the name with its possessive s supplies its letters

explanation.surface: Alan's living-room sofa set is finished off with some scatter cushions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scatter cushions' is a familiar phrase that hides the split: 'scatter' is the anagram signal and 'cushions' the verb definition. 'Top off' turns ALANS into LANS.
explanation.definitionFit: To cushion something is to protect it from shock, just as wrapping or padding it protects it.

clue.text: Admiring Raphael's representation of a relationship

indicators.note: the possessive says these letters belong within the words before it, held by the painter's name

parts.note: the last letter of the first word and the start of the painter's name run together

explanation.surface: Someone admires a painting by the Renaissance artist Raphael.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no hiding word as such; 'Raphael's representation' teases that the letters belong to the painter's work.
explanation.definitionFit: A chart plotting how one variable changes with another is a visual depiction of a relationship.

clue.text: Deadlock when one politician confronts idiot online

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
MP, a Member of Parliament
an ass is a fool
E is the prefix for electronic or online, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: Talks stall when an MP clashes with a fool on social media.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation where no progress is possible because neither side yields is a stalemate or standstill.

clue.text: Bad breath: has taken tablet or tisane?

indicators.note: the rearranged word takes in the pill, holding it inside
bad suggests something gone wrong, so the letters of the next word are spoilt into another order

parts.note: E is slang for an ecstasy tablet

explanation.surface: Someone with halitosis wonders whether a pill or an infusion would help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' rearranges BREATH into HERBTA, and 'has taken' places E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An infusion made from leaves or flowers rather than tea is this drink, the French term being tisane.

clue.text: Carefree as a glamper appears to be

definitions.text: as a glamper appears to be
definitions.meaning: a lamp, a source of illumination, sits at the heart of the word glamper

explanation.surface: A glamorous camper looks happy and relaxed.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is cryptic: the middle of gLAMPer is LAMP, so the word glamper is 'light-centred'. Glamping is luxury camping.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cheerful and without worries is the plain sense of the adjective, a synonym of carefree.

clue.text: Passes by Italian man when cycling

indicators.note: cycling moves a letter round from one end of the word to the other

parts.note: signore is the Italian for a gentleman

explanation.surface: An Italian gentleman rides past on his bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when cycling' sends the S at the front of SIGNORE round to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: To disregard someone or something is to let it pass by without attention.

clue.text: Look less English, after putting on the Spanish clothes

indicators.note: the Spanish article is put on, added after the shortened verb
less means without, so one letter is dropped from the verb

parts.note: to look a certain way is to appear
el is the Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Someone tries to look less English by dressing in Spanish clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less English' takes E out of APPEAR, leaving APPAR; EL is then added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Garments in general, especially as sold, are a formal synonym for clothing.

clue.text: Girl, 8, unhappy with bad charging unit

indicators.note: unhappy suggests something disturbed, so these letters are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: the numeral is written out as a word to supply its letters

explanation.surface: A sad eight-year-old girl is unhappy and naughty.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 8 is not a cross-reference but the number itself; 'unhappy' rearranges GIRL, EIGHT and BAD.
explanation.definitionFit: The cavalry regiment famed in Tennyson's poem for its disastrous charge at Balaclava is a charging unit.

clue.text: Real leather or artificial leather? Both satisfy the requirements for this bag

definitions.text: Real leather or artificial leather? Both satisfy the requirements for this bag

parts.words: Real leather or artificial leather? Both satisfy the requirements for this bag
parts.note: each phrase contains the three letters a, l, l across its two words, so each one holds a word meaning everything

explanation.surface: A shopper asks whether a travel bag should be genuine or faux leather.
explanation.walkthrough: Look inside 'reAL Leather' and 'artificiAL Leather': both contain ALL, and so each 'holds ALL', which names the bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A large soft travel bag that takes everything a traveller needs is called this, a carryall.

clue.text: One identifying Twitter topic that has Henry reeling, aghast

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

indicators.note: reeling means staggering about, so the word's letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A trending topic on Twitter leaves someone called Henry shocked and unsteady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Henry' looks like a person in the surface; it is the unit of inductance, symbol H.
explanation.definitionFit: On social media a word preceded by the # symbol labels and groups posts on one subject.

clue.text: Near neighbours buried in churchyard

definitions.meaning: close at hand, within easy reach
in the middle of churchyard two letters stand side by side, an aitch next to a wye, so the phrase names that adjacent pair linked by a word meaning plus

explanation.surface: Graves of people who lived next door lie close together in the churchyard.
explanation.walkthrough: In churcHYard the letters H and Y are neighbours; read the answer as a phrase joining those two letters with the word for plus.
explanation.definitionFit: Something close at hand and easy to reach is conveniently near, an informal adjective sense.

clue.text: Formally present sailor as one on board that's seasoned?

parts.note: to table a motion or proposal is to present it formally for discussion
an old salt is an experienced sailor

explanation.surface: An experienced mariner is formally introduced aboard ship as a seasoned hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'board' is the dining table rather than a ship's deck, and 'seasoned' plays on a veteran sailor while meaning it gives food its seasoning.
explanation.definitionFit: The fine white condiment set on the dinner table, the board, is what gives food its seasoning.

clue.text: Retail outlet applying charges by type of story?

parts.note: the police book a suspect when they formally record a charge against them
a tall story is an unlikely, exaggerated tale

explanation.surface: A shop seems to set its prices by the genre of fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand or kiosk selling printed volumes, as at a railway station, is a small retail outlet.

clue.text: A new clue a setter's trying out, for starters or an appetizer

parts.note: a tip is a hint or clue

indicators.note: for starters means taking the opening letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: A setter tests a fresh clue, as a little something to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for starters' picks A, S, T, O from 'a setter's trying out'. 'starters' also hints at the course itself.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian course of cold meats and vegetables served before the main meal is a starter.

clue.text: Anxiety is rising in one part of joint

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the carpentry term

parts.note: a tenon is the projecting piece of a mortise-and-tenon woodworking joint

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means read upwards, so the little word is turned backwards

explanation.surface: Stress is mounting in an aching joint of the body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' suggests a knee or elbow, but it is a woodworking joint: the mortise and tenon.
explanation.definitionFit: Nervous strain and mental stress, a feeling of unease, is a synonym for anxiety.

clue.text: Piggy, initially patronised on requesting conch, is nobbled eventually

indicators.note: initially tells us to take the first letter of each of the seven words that follow

explanation.surface: Piggy, the character in Lord of the Flies, is talked down to when asking for the conch, and finally overpowered.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls Golding's novel, in which Piggy holds the conch to speak and is killed.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective meaning of or like swine, the porky resemblance being in looks or habits.

clue.text: "One with long neck and rounded body" only partially describes it, arguably

definitions.text: One with long neck and rounded body

indicators.note: only partially says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A quoted description is said to give only a partial account of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted phrase is the definition; 'only partially' signals that the answer lies within 'describeS IT, ARguably'.
explanation.definitionFit: This Indian stringed instrument has a long fretted neck and a gourd-shaped resonating body.

clue.text: Seconds? Eating a thin slice

parts.note: having a meal means eating it

explanation.surface: A diner asks for a second helping while eating a sliver.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin paring or curl cut off a surface, as of wood or cheese, is a sliver.

clue.text: Weapon detective found upside-down in river

indicators.note: in places the inverted detective inside the river's name

parts.note: the Trent is a major river in the English Midlands

indicators.note: in a down entry, upside-down means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: A murder weapon is found by a detective in a river where the body was dumped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upside-down' suits a down entry, where reading a word backwards means reading it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-pronged spear, as carried by Neptune or a Roman gladiator, is a weapon.

clue.text: Having an office under the vacated complex

indicators.note: a vacated word has been emptied, so only its outside letters remain
complex means intricate or mixed up, so the letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone has an office beneath an empty building complex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacated' empties THE to TE; 'complex' then rearranges UNDER with TE.
explanation.definitionFit: A post held permanently, especially an academic one, is held with tenure, so the holder occupies an office.

clue.text: What might get you jiggling two bits in nudist colony?

indicators.note: two bits in says only two short runs from within the phrase are kept, one from each word, and the rest of its letters go

parts.note: the phrase supplies its letters, from which the two inner runs are kept

explanation.surface: A naturist camp might set people wobbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jiggling' suggests bare bodies wobbling in the surface; in the cryptic reading it is dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: A dance club or party where people dance to pop music gets people moving and jiggling.

clue.text: Economical health resort used by band

parts.note: a spa is a resort with mineral springs
a ring is a band, as worn on a finger

explanation.surface: A thrifty health spa is used by a pop group.
explanation.definitionFit: Being frugal and careful with resources is the adjective's sense, a synonym of thrifty.

clue.text: Worships one getting into beards

indicators.note: getting into tells us the numeral goes inside the verb meaning confronts

parts.note: to beard someone is to defy or confront them boldly
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A worshipper grows a beard, as some religious devotees do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beards' looks like facial hair but is the verb, to confront.
explanation.definitionFit: To regard someone as a god and adore them is a step beyond venerating, an extreme form of worship.

clue.text: Some Arak, if an odd bit of it gets Denise drunk

parts.note: it refers back to the spirit named earlier; its odd-numbered letters are both A, so one odd letter is A

indicators.note: drunk suggests confusion, so the woman's name is jumbled into another order

explanation.surface: A woman named Denise gets drunk on the Middle Eastern spirit arak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' points back to Arak in the definition; its first and third letters are both A, so either gives the odd bit.
explanation.definitionFit: Arak is an anise-flavoured spirit, so the seed flavouring is part of what goes into it.

clue.text: A broken leg? No getaway for Lucifer

indicators.note: broken means smashed apart, so these letters are reassembled in another order

parts.note: flight is escape, a getaway

explanation.surface: A thief with a broken leg can't make a getaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges LEG and NO into NGELO.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucifer was the brightest angel before his fall, his name meaning bearer of light in Latin.
